clue.text: It's fatal to bring an end to hostilities with an ill-tempered speech

parts.note: death is the end of a life
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: A warning that an angry speech could reignite a conflict with deadly results.
explanation.walkthrough: The small word 'to' between the end and hostilities just strings the first two pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: A death warrant is the official order authorising an execution, so the document itself is lethal.

clue.text: Lasting change to bad rule

indicators.note: to change something is to alter its make-up, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A call for permanent reform of an unjust regulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something durable endures and keeps going a long time, which is what lasting means.

clue.text: Certain to be terribly rude to stupid fellow

indicators.note: something done terribly is done badly, so the word beside it comes out jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is bound to be very rude to an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled word is attached to the fool, so the fool comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Assured and certain are synonyms, both meaning confident or guaranteed beyond doubt.

clue.text: Record collector played this on air

indicators.note: a piece played is performed in a new way, so these letters are rendered in a different order

explanation.surface: A vinyl enthusiast hears a track spun on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record collector' suggests someone with shelves of LPs; here the records are historical ones, compiled by a scholar of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A historian gathers and preserves records of past events, a playful reading of collecting records.

clue.text: Dreadful gag leads to endless row stirred up by troublemakers

definitions.note: a description of the noun: trouble stirred up by troublemakers

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the following word is jumbled
without an end means the final letter of the next word is dropped

explanation.surface: A bad joke sparks a quarrel among rowdy hooligans.
explanation.walkthrough: AGGRO is British slang, short for aggravation, for aggressive or violent behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is informal British slang for hostility and trouble, exactly what troublemakers stir up.

clue.text: Australian creature rest mistook for a bird

indicators.note: a mistaken reading gets things in the wrong order, so the preceding word is scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone resting confuses a kangaroo with a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male chicken, a farmyard fowl and so a kind of bird.

clue.text: New student acquires a book

explanation.surface: A fresh pupil gets hold of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, from the plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a short novel, so it is a kind of book of fiction.

clue.text: He traces source of drink to quartet in US restaurant

indicators.note: being in a place means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

explanation.surface: A man follows the origin of his beverage to four people in an American eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman four goes inside the eatery after the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A water diviner, or dowser, locates underground springs with a forked stick, tracking down a hidden supply.

clue.text: Checks made by the police

definitions.meaning: first meaning: halts or stops progress

definitions.note: describes the plural noun: things made by the police
definitions.meaning: second meaning: what officers make when they detain suspects

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it suggests police inspections; split, it gives a verb and a noun sharing one spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest growth is to halt it, and police make arrests when they take people into custody.

clue.text: Bearing marks of a routine day

parts.note: stuck in a groove means stuck in a rut

explanation.surface: Signs of an ordinary, humdrum day.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grooved has channels or furrows cut into it, carrying visible lines on its surface.

clue.text: School staff sailed out after meal

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the word before it is rearranged

explanation.surface: Teachers set off on a boat trip after eating.
explanation.walkthrough: Dinner ladies are the women who serve lunch in British schools; 'after' puts the jumbled word behind the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner ladies are employed by British schools to serve and supervise pupils' lunches, so they count among school staff.

clue.text: Ban me on return to drinking place, then leave

indicators.note: returning means coming back the way you went, so the word before is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone is barred from the pub when they come back and is told to go.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official prohibition, especially on trade, which is a formal ban.

clue.text: Bird table delicacy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small European bunting
second meaning: the same bird eaten as a gourmet dish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird table' suggests a garden feeder, but the words split into a bird and a dining delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small songbird traditionally eaten whole as a prized French gourmet dish.

clue.text: Extreme fear about parent coming round

indicators.note: coming round something means encircling it, so one piece wraps the other

explanation.surface: Terror at the thought of a parent turning up.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great apprehension or terror, an intense and overpowering kind of fright.

clue.text: Anger resulted as I spoilt fun by including one in class

indicators.note: including means holding within, so one piece goes inside another
something spoilt is ruined, so the letters around it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone got cross after a spoilsport ruined the fun in a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' looks like a classroom, but it is a grade or rating.
explanation.definitionFit: To infuriate is to make someone furious, a verb meaning to enrage or anger them.

clue.text: Open exchange leads to unrestrained business

explanation.surface: A frank conversation results in uncontrolled commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: Free trade is commerce between countries without tariffs or barriers, an unrestricted market of goods.

clue.text: One taking law into his own hands to cast out evil giant

definitions.text: One taking law into his own hands

indicators.note: metal cast out is poured into a new mould, so the letters take a new shape

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale hero expels a wicked giant without waiting for the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast out' reads as banishing the giant; it is the signal to rearrange the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigilante punishes wrongdoers personally, acting without legal authority instead of relying on courts.

clue.text: Travel by stream with a forest dweller

parts.note: a rill is a small brook

explanation.surface: A journey along a brook alongside someone who lives in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas are great apes living in the tropical rainforests of central Africa.

clue.text: Turn up for US writer to be taken in by fat cat

indicators.note: being taken in means being received inside, so one piece sits within the other
in a down clue turning up means reading from the bottom upwards, so the word is backwards

explanation.surface: A surprise as an American author is fooled by a wealthy fat cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat cat' reads as a rich person, but the words are split: fat is the outer piece, cat the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The leopard is a large spotted wild feline of Africa and Asia, one of the big cats.

clue.text: Be superior to former church student

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Outdoing a one-time divinity student.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the Church of England; L is the learner plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel over others is to outdo or surpass them, which means being better than they are.

clue.text: Clear impression formed after I've reflected

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is flipped, so the word before it is read backwards

parts.note: a dent is a hollow pressed into a surface

explanation.surface: Someone forms a clear view of things after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflected' suggests thinking things over; here it means mirrored.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident and clear are synonyms meaning plainly obvious and easily seen or understood.

clue.text: Cogitate afresh when one leaves home

indicators.note: doing something afresh means doing it again in a new way, so the letters are rearranged
the Roman one departing means a letter i is removed

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, less one

explanation.surface: Think things over again once a family member has moved out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small house, typically in the countryside, and so a place to live.

clue.text: Anxious over disturbance in student union

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the jumbled piece sits within the union

parts.note: the National Union of Students, the UK students' body

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so the word before it is jumbled

explanation.surface: Worry about trouble breaking out at the students' union.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous means uneasy and apprehensive, a close synonym for being worried or anxious.

clue.text: Point to bird at back end of ship

explanation.surface: Pointing out a seabird perched at the rear of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rearmost part of a vessel, opposite the bow at the front.

clue.text: Perverse to have danced?

definitions.note: a past participle: having done the twist
definitions.meaning: second meaning: performed the 1960s dance the twist

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second sense: the twist is a dance, so to have danced it is to have twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: Twisted describes a warped, unhealthy mind, and is also the past form of the dance named the twist.

clue.text: Catch a film?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lever or catch that frees a mechanism
second meaning: a film newly put out in cinemas

explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch a film' reads as going to see a movie; split, a catch is a release mechanism and a new movie is a release.
explanation.definitionFit: A release is a device that unfastens something, and also a newly issued movie or record.

clue.text: Mean to get girl in the course of time

indicators.note: something happening in the course of a period falls within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: an age is a long period

explanation.surface: Intending to find a girlfriend eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb meaning intend; it is the statistical mean.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic the mean is the sum divided by the count, the usual sense of average.

clue.text: Focus on grounds for growing concern

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece being on another means it follows it

explanation.surface: Concentrate on the reasons for a worry that is getting bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing concern' sounds like mounting worry; it is a business that sells plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden centre is a shop selling plants and gardening supplies, literally a company about growing things.
